thread:
Maya: seeing an eviction wave in eu-west1 around 02:10, lots of tiny-gang pods bounced. anyone else?
Jon: yup, noticed ~200 small inference pods rescheduled in 3 AZs.
Li: looks like thermal mitigation kicked on a subset of racks -> node drained -> pods evicted -> schedulerspread created fragmentation.
Maya: link to flamegraph/metrics?
Li: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/rack/evicts?from=1715009000 (will share screenshot)
Sam: heap of short msgs but root cause seems to be rack-level NIC cooldown + thermal fan ramp. nodes marked NotReady?
Paul: nodes went NotReady for ~45s then kubelet drained them, preemptions showed up as "Evicted" not preempt.
Maya: sample kubelet logs:```
Mar 21 02:10:12 node-az1-04 kubelet: NodeNotReady: thermal: fan_ctl engaged
Mar 21 02:10:13 node-az1-04 kubelet: Pod eviction started: memory pressure false, disk pressure false, scheduling false
```
Jon: scheduler scoring favored intra-rack NVLink locality; when racks evaporate we end up with tiny islands that block gang pods.
Li: and our warm pools are per-AZ, not per-rack -> can't backfill within same NVLink group.
Sam: cost question: we used spot-heavy SKU in eu-west1c for those racks, so rebalancing spilled to more expensive on-demand pools by burst.
Maya: any short-term mitigation we can flip?
Paul: 1) lower topology affinity weight for NVLink for tiny-gang jobs (quick) 2) increase warm-pool replication across racks (takes provisioning time) 3) descheduler run to coalesce pods onto fewer racks once nodes heal (can cause churn).
Li: also reduce per-pod gpu request for microworkers from 0.25 -> 0.125 where safe (trades throughput for higher packing).
Jon: I can push a canary to reweight scheduler plugin to -5 NVLink preference for tiny-gang class. what metric should we watch?
Maya: watch pending pod count, eviction rate, and tail latency for tiny-gang traces. set alert threshold: evictions > 50/min for 5m.
Sam: script to temporarily taint thermal-affected nodes so scheduler avoids them instead of kubelet draining:```bash
kubectl taint nodes node-az1-04 thermal=hot:NoSchedule --overwrite
```
Paul: careful: tainting prevents graceful reschedule to nearby nodes; use for immediate stopgap only.
Li: longer term: adjust warm pool placement to be rack-aware and implement soft-affinity for NVLink locality that can be relaxed under thermal events. also consider a "rack-quarantine" descheduler that avoids spreading tiny-gang across too many racks.
Jon: opening a quick RFC for scheduler change and a runbook for thermal drain events.
Maya: can someone own the runbook update and the emergency canary? @Jon?
Jon: I got the canary, will roll - canary id: deploy-thermal-171500-01. sched-bot: starting canary rollout. :rocket:
sched-bot: [deploy-thermal-171500-01] 1/3 hosts updated -> monitoring hooks attached
Sam: rolling the taint on the 3 most flaky nodes in eu-west1c now.
Li: postmortem notes: thermal events are correlated with nightly maintenance starting at 02:00 in that region. Ops sched needs to shift maintenance window or stagger across racks.
Maya: good catch. ops, can we move maintenance by 2h or stagger? @Paul can you coordinate with infra ops?
Paul: yep i'll ping ops and propose 04:00 stagger.
Maya: thanks all. we'll reconvene after canary completes and if evictions drop. :thumbsup:
